name: Apache Hudi
model: Open table format for upserts and incremental pulls: tables as Parquet base files plus log files and a timeline of commits
engine_note: Not a server: Parquet (plus Avro log) files in object storage with a commit timeline; record-key index makes upserts and deletes cheap
consistency: Snapshot isolation between writers, readers and table services. Single writer by default; multiple writers need optimistic concurrency with a lock provider (ZooKeeper, DynamoDB...), or 1.0's non-blocking mode. Commits are per table.
scaling: Storage scales with object storage; compute is Spark, Flink, Trino, Hive and others; background compaction and clustering run as table services.
reach: Reach for it when you stream change data (CDC) into a data lake and need frequent upserts and incremental reads of what changed.
avoid: Avoid for append-only or small data, or if your engines lack good Hudi support; Iceberg has broader engine adoption.
escape: streaming upserts into a large data lake that a single database could not hold
chat: CDC copy of the messages table streamed into the lake with upserts, for analytics and training sets.
notes: Table format, not a server. Concurrency from the Hudi concurrency control page (fetched 2026-10-04). Managed offerings (Onehouse, Amazon EMR bundling Hudi) not re-fetched today; unconfirmed in this pass. 'Iceberg has broader engine adoption' is a judgement, not a sourced fact.
